rv.q: Whatever the reason, Henrik Ibsen's 1891. Hedda Gabler , now onstage with the Artistic Home at the Den under the muscular direction of Monica Payne, feels vital and enraging.
Brookelyn Hébert’s portrayal of Ibsen’s celebrated femme fatale is an old-school, eyeball-grabbing star turn, one that every theater lover will relish.
Monica Payne’s direction is sure and moves the action smoothly around the multi-level set.
The Artistic Home’s production of ‘Hedda Gabler’ is a good reminder of why classics should be seen every so often.
It is wonderful to look at and even better to experience.
If you love the work and want to see a finely acted production, this version of Hedda would be a good fit for you.

The technical aspects of the production are flawless with costumes (Rachel Lambert), sound (Petter Wahlback), lighting (Rachel Levy) and props (Randy Rozier) all working to fit together and keep the flow and story on track.
If you are a lover of classic theater interested in experiencing an excellent story written by a master playwright this production offers a rare opportunity.

cn.t: Critics praise this vital, muscular production of Ibsen's classic, with Brookelyn Hébert's commanding performance as Hedda anchoring a diabolically humorous adaptation that feels urgently relevant today, despite occasional unevenness.
